<div class="funmel-hero">
<p class="funmel-eyebrow">REAL DATA · EIGHT ORIGINAL PHOTOGRAPHS · TWO MATCHING SETS</p>
<p class="funmel-lead">From the original photograph to a traceable comparison.</p>
<p>A complete practice run with supplied metadata, five spots per target colony,
image QC, matched coefficients, saved tables and publication-format exports.</p>
</div>

Start here after [installing FunMel](FunMel.html). Run numbered steps in order;
all objects used below are created in this article. The figures and tables shown
here are generated from the bundled photographs during rendering. The
[function catalog](Function-examples.html) covers specialist tools separately.

## What this experiment contains

Each matching set has **one independent control plate and three independent
confrontation plates**. Each plate has four target *Zymoseptoria tritici* colonies.
Confrontation plates also contain a central fungus and connected hyphal growth;
control plates do not. The central growth is not an inhibition zone.

| Matching set | Independent plate image | Role | Replicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A60_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_38.JPG | A60_2 confrontation | 1 |
| A60_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_39.JPG | A60_2 confrontation | 2 |
| A60_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_40.JPG | A60_2 confrontation | 3 |
| A60_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_41.JPG | Own-set control | 1 |
| B20_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_42.JPG | B20_2 confrontation | 1 |
| B20_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_43.JPG | B20_2 confrontation | 2 |
| B20_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_44.JPG | B20_2 confrontation | 3 |
| B20_2_14_days | 2026_10_02_99_45.JPG | Own-set control | 1 |

The folder-derived labels are teaching labels whose biological identities and
assignments must be checked against laboratory records. The supplied source
field `fungus="hm83"` is retained without assigning an unverified biological role.
Unrecorded strain/medium fields remain blank. The eight original JPEGs are
unchanged. No separate image download is required.

<div class="funmel-note"><strong>Units matter.</strong> This is eight plates,
32 target colonies and, when all requested spots fit, 160 spots. It is not 160
independent biological replicates. One control per set supports descriptive
coefficients, not the package's replicated-cell significance tests.</div>

## 1. Locate the photographs and create one practice project

```{r prepare14}
library(FunMel)
photos14 <- system.file("extdata","14-days",package="FunMel")
stopifnot(nzchar(photos14))
project_dir14 <- tempfile("FunMel_14_day_project_")
project14 <- prepare_experiment(photos14,project_dir14)
```

`tempfile()` supplies a **new temporary folder name**, so this teaching run does
not overwrite earlier work. Its files last only as long as the temporary
location remains. For a project you want to keep, replace that assignment
**before starting** with a new durable folder, for example:

```{r durable-folder, eval=FALSE}
# Alternative to tempfile() above; use a new folder once.
project_dir14 <- file.path(path.expand("~"),"FunMel_14_day_project")
project14 <- prepare_experiment(photos14,project_dir14)
```

Do not run both preparation alternatives for the same project. To revisit work
already saved, go directly to step 8. A folder or ZIP is passed directly here;
there is no file chooser and no opportunity to select a QC image accidentally.

```{r paths14, eval=FALSE}
project14$project_dir   # All output files.
project14$metadata_file # Project copy of the experimental design.
project14$qc_dir        # QC PNGs created by the image run.
```

## 2. Check the supplied metadata

The combined metadata is discovered automatically. Inspect it before measuring:

```{r metadata14}
metadata14 <- read.csv(project14$metadata_file,check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(metadata14[,c("plate_id","set_id","treatment","centre_model","replicate")],
             row.names=FALSE)
validate_metadata(metadata14)
```

Each control appears once, labelled `treatment="control"` and
`centre_model="none"`. Each confrontation uses `centre_model="fungus"`.
All four plates in a matching group share their `set_id`. A60_2 never uses
B20_2's control or vice versa. `replicate` is numbered within a treatment and
set; it does not by itself pair a treatment plate with a uniquely replicated
control. With one control in a set, its mean is the shared denominator for the
three treatment plates.

Verify treatment identities, controls, sets, day and any recorded strain/medium.
Only correct information that is missing or inaccurate; **no FALSE-to-TRUE
approval edits are required**. Your own additional columns remain preserved.
Do not infer biological identities from a filename alone. If corrections are
needed, edit the project CSV and save it before the next step. Do not change
image identity or layout after analysis without remeasuring.

## 3. Set calibration and measure all eight plates

For this rendered teaching run, `90` is an **illustrative outer dish diameter**,
not a verified physical measurement of these photographs. Replace it with the
actual outer diameter for scientific use. Do not paste subsequent R commands
into a `readline()` prompt; this workflow sets the number directly.

```{r measure14}
dish_mm <- 90
result14 <- run_experiment(
  project14,dish_diameter_mm=dish_mm,max_dim=1200,
  n_spots=5,spot_radius_mm=0.4,n_boot=20
)
result14$analysis_status
result14$failed
stopifnot(nrow(result14$failed)==0L)
```

The expected status is `"complete"`; the failure table has zero rows. This saves
`image_analysis.rds`, measurement CSVs and a QC PNG for each plate. A genuine
failed image must be corrected before finalization. Success does not certify
segmentation or biological accuracy.

| Setting | Meaning in this tutorial |
|---|---|
| `dish_diameter_mm` | Outer diameter used to convert pixels to millimetres |
| `max_dim=1200` | Longest working-image dimension; influences spatial resolution |
| `n_spots=5` | Request five additional circular regions within each target colony |
| `spot_radius_mm=0.4` | Radius of each spot, not its diameter |
| `n_boot=20` | Quick teaching setting for spatial-block bootstrap summaries, not precise uncertainty |

Whole-colony MI uses eligible interior pixels, excluding the rim and
saturated/specular pixels. Spots add a deterministic, spatially spread sample;
they do not replace whole-colony measurements. Omit spot settings for
whole-colony measurements alone. Use consistent settings across comparable plates.

```{r counts14}
data.frame(plates=nrow(result14$plates),colonies=nrow(result14$colonies),
           spots=nrow(result14$spots),failed=nrow(result14$failed))
```

## 4. Inspect masks, spots and illumination

Inspect all eight QC images in `project14$qc_dir`. The examples below show one
confrontation and its own control; they do not replace reviewing the remaining
photographs.

```{r qc14, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5, dpi=120, fig.cap="Example QC: a confrontation plate and its own matching control. Inspect the target outlines, spot locations, central fungal tissue/hyphae and dish calibration on every image.", out.width="100%"}
qc14 <- file.path(project14$qc_dir,c("2026_10_02_99_38_qc.png","2026_10_02_99_41_qc.png"))
for(qc_image in qc14) {
  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(qc_image))
}
```

Check target-colony boundaries, central tissue/hyphal separation, spot containment,
dish edge, shadows, glare and warning text. The approximately round targets need
not have perfectly circular outlines. Correct unsuitable images or measurements
before interpreting the final comparisons.

```{r illumination14}
knitr::kable(result14$plates[,c("plate_id","n_colonies_detected",
  "central_detected","flat_field_status")],row.names=FALSE)
```

These photographs produce `flat_field_status="withheld_degenerate_fit"`:
the fitted illumination correction did not pass the saturation safeguard and
was withheld. This is an informative status, **not evidence of adequate
illumination**. Treatment/control ratios do not guarantee cancellation of
exposure or lighting differences. Use consistent imaging and a suitable reference;
rephotograph when needed. The figures here illustrate software output, not a
validated melanin-concentration assay.

FunMel prints reminders and warns about unconfirmed image QC. Default computation
continues without editing review flags. Expected reminder warnings are omitted
from this rendered article for readability; they are explained here and remain
visible in a normal console run.

## 5. Inspect whole-colony, spot and profile tables

```{r colony-table14}
knitr::kable(head(result14$colonies[,c("plate_id","colony_id","MI_min",
  "MI_mean","MI_max","MI_spot_mean","n_spots_measured","spot_status")]),digits=2,
  row.names=FALSE)
```

`MI = 100 - CIELAB L*`; larger values indicate darker tissue. `MI_min` and
`MI_max` are observed whole-colony pixel extrema, not confidence limits.
`MI_spot_mean` is the mean of the individual spot means. The corresponding
`MI_spot_min/max` are extrema of **spot means**, not pixel extrema.

```{r spot-table14}
knitr::kable(head(result14$spots[,c("plate_id","colony_id","spot_id",
  "spot_radius_mm","n_pixels","MI_mean","MI_min","MI_max")]),digits=2,
  row.names=FALSE)
```

Each spot has a location in working-image pixels (`x_px`, `y_px`), a physical
radius and an achieved pixel count. `L_mean` is mean CIELAB lightness; spot
`MI_mean` is `100-L_mean`. Pixel counts depend on the scale and working resolution.
Check `spot_status` and `n_spots_measured`; if all requested spots cannot fit
without overlap, the incomplete summary is unavailable instead of invented.

```{r profiles14}
knitr::kable(head(result14$profiles[,intersect(c("plate_id","colony_id","mid_mm",
  "MI_mean","MI_lo","MI_hi"),names(result14$profiles))]),digits=2,row.names=FALSE)
```

Profiles describe darkness from the colony edge inward. Their spatial bootstrap
bounds quantify an image-level sampling procedure, not biological replication
or chemical melanin uncertainty. The low bootstrap count here is for speed.

The full metadata is in `result14$metadata`; custom column names and values are
retained. Colliding measurement names receive a `metadata_` prefix only in
measurement tables. Do not use `project14$result_file$spots`: `result_file` is
a **filename**, whereas `result14$spots` is a **data frame**.

## 6. Finalize and verify the own-control arithmetic

```{r finish14}
reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14)
knitr::kable(reviewed14$melanization_coefficient[,c("set_id","treatment",
  "MI_treatment_mean","MI_control_mean","melanization_coefficient",
  "n_treatment_plates","n_control_plates")],digits=3,row.names=FALSE)
reviewed14$assessment$status
```

A plate's MI is the equally weighted mean of its target-colony `MI_mean` values.
Within each set, the coefficient is:

\[
\mathrm{MC}_{s,t}=\frac{\operatorname{mean}(\mathrm{MI}_{\text{treatment plates},s,t})}
{\operatorname{mean}(\mathrm{MI}_{\text{control plates},s})}.
\]

For this teaching calibration, A60_2 is approximately **1.628** and B20_2
approximately **1.302**. Verify the saved arithmetic without pooling controls:

```{r arithmetic14}
cf14 <- reviewed14$melanization_coefficient
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(cf14$melanization_coefficient,
                           cf14$MI_treatment_mean/cf14$MI_control_mean)))
knitr::kable(reviewed14$per_plate_coefficients,digits=3,row.names=FALSE)
```

The status `"insufficient_plate_replication"` is expected. There is one control
per set, so significance tests are withheld, while valid descriptive ratios
remain available. Four colonies and five spots per colony do not add independent
control plates. These two treatments also occur in different sets, so a direct
causal treatment ranking may be confounded with batch. A darker image-based mean
is not a demonstrated fold change in melanin concentration.

For a prespecified spot-mean descriptive response:

```{r spot-ratio14, eval=FALSE}
spot_coefficient14 <- melanization_coefficient(reviewed14,response="MI_spot_mean")
```

This changes the response definition; it does not create independent spot
replicates. The default figure and assessment use whole-colony MI.

## 7. Display, export and explain the final figure

```{r comparison14, fig.height=5.5, fig.cap="Descriptive real-data comparison. Each row uses that treatment's own set control; these are image-darkness ratios under the illustrative calibration."}
print(plot_treatment_comparison(project14))
```

You can also plot the finalized object already in memory:

```{r comparison-object14, eval=FALSE}
print(plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed14))
```

- **Left panel:** independent plate MI means. Squares are controls; coloured
  circles are treatment plates; lower diamonds are treatment means.
- **Right panel:** each treatment plate divided by its own set's control mean,
  and the set-level ratio of means. The dashed reference line is MC = 1.
- **Bars and printed ± values:** one between-plate SD, not confidence intervals.
  Control SD is unavailable for a single control. Ratio SD conditions on the
  shared control mean and does not include its uncertainty.
- **QC reminders:** remain visible in the console and separate caption file; they
  are not processing failures or automatic approval. Inspect the images before reporting results.

Finalization already exported `treatment_comparison.pdf`, `.svg`, `.png` and
`_statistics.csv` into the project folder. To create a named alternative:

```{r export14, eval=FALSE}
plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed14,
  file=file.path(project14$project_dir,"my_14_day_comparison"),
  labels=c(A60_2="Fungal treatment A60_2",B20_2="Fungal treatment B20_2"))
```

PDF and SVG retain vector text and geometry; PNG is 600 dpi. Check the target
journal's final dimensions, font sizes and caption requirements. Changing display
labels does not change metadata or statistical matching.

## 8. Close R, reopen the project and read saved tables

For a project saved in a durable folder, start a fresh session and run:

```{r resume14, eval=FALSE}
library(FunMel)
project14 <- load_experiment() # Select project.rds in its current folder.
result14 <- read_experiment(project14)
reviewed14 <- read_experiment(project14,finalized=TRUE)
head(result14$spots)
print(plot_treatment_comparison(project14))
```

To update final outputs after correcting valid experimental annotations:

```{r refinish14, eval=FALSE}
reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14)
```

`Final outputs saved` means this succeeded. It is unnecessary to prepare the
photographs again. Keep the complete folder, including project.rds, metadata CSV
and saved results. `load_experiment()` reconnects moved internal paths. Saved
measurements can be read/finalized without the original photographs, but a new
image run still needs them. Missing metadata cannot be safely guessed or rebuilt
from image appearance. Changes affecting masks require reanalysis.

## 9. Optional close-up measurements and specialist tools

Batch results keep tables and saved QC PNGs but drop large image arrays. For
interactive image-level views, reprocess just one real photograph with images
retained:

```{r detail14, eval=FALSE}
row14 <- metadata14[metadata14$plate_id=="2026_10_02_99_38",,drop=FALSE]
plate14 <- analyze_plate(file.path(project14$image_root,row14$relative_file),
  id=row14$plate_id,layout=layout_by_treatment(row14),dish_diameter_mm=dish_mm,
  max_dim=1200,n_spots=5,spot_radius_mm=0.4,n_boot=20,keep_images=TRUE)
plot_qc(plate14)
print(plot_profiles(plate14))
plot_melanization_map(plate14,type="2d")
```

The darkness map is not pigment concentration. For a different spot count/radius,
`sample_colony_spots(plate14,n_spots=3,spot_radius_mm=0.4)` demonstrates the
sampling API; do not change compared responses inconsistently. Calibration,
classifier training and interactive annotation examples are in the
[complete function catalog](Function-examples.html). A classifier trained on
synthetic teaching labels is not validated for these photographs.

## Find the exported files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| project.rds | Project paths; reopen with load_experiment() |
| plate_metadata.csv | Editable experimental assignments, one row per plate |
| image_analysis.rds | Original measured tables and analysis status |
| colonies.csv, spots.csv, profiles.csv, plates.csv | Measurement tables |
| failed.csv | Failed-image reports; zero rows on a successful run |
| metadata_used.csv | Full metadata attached to the outputs |
| reviewed_analysis.rds | Finalized result; the name does not certify review |
| assessment.rds | Statistical/descriptive assessment and its status |
| melanization_coefficient.csv | Own-set ratios of treatment/control means |
| per_plate_coefficients.csv | Treatment plate ratios using own-set control means |
| coefficient_plate_means.csv | Independent plate means used in calculations |
| treatment_comparison.pdf/.svg/.png | Comparison exports |
| treatment_comparison_statistics.csv | Exact descriptive values plotted |
| treatment_comparison_caption.txt | Full interpretation, SD definitions, limitations and QC status |
| qc_review_status.csv | Recorded QC status, with no default approval requirement |
| qc/ | One QC PNG per image |
| sessionInfo.txt | R, platform and package versions |

Different recorded day/strain/medium contexts create separate final output
folders and `context_index.csv`; do not pool incompatible contexts. To adapt
this tutorial to other photographs, replace the input folder/ZIP and verified
metadata, retaining the own-control design. Do not reuse these eight-file labels
for another experiment.

The installed script `examples/walkthrough_14_days.R` follows the same numbered
procedure. Precomputed tables in `extdata/14_day_example` have their own
`PROVENANCE.md`; they are illustrative measurements, not ground truth. This
rendered tutorial recomputes the photographs and does not substitute those tables.

The comparison figure has **no text paragraph underneath by default**. Full
interpretation is saved separately as `treatment_comparison_caption.txt` during
export and is retained in the plot's `FunMel_caption` attribute. Use
`plot_treatment_comparison(project14,caption="brief")` for a short embedded note,
or `caption="full"` for the full caption. Removing figure text does not remove
QC warnings, matching checks or replication safeguards.
